text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.2% today as oil prices spiked on geopolitical tensions—Brent crude hit $113, the highest since May, after reports that the U.S. plans to resume strikes against Iran and has pulled diplomats from Saudi Arabia over Houthi attacks. While higher crude prices typically help refiners by widening their profit margins, the sharp jump driven by regional conflict and political uncertainty often spooks equity markets broadly, weighing on energy stocks even as the underlying commodity moves higher.

The refining backdrop is mixed: refineries are running at 93.4% capacity and oil inventories remain elevated at 695 million barrels, which limits how much margin pressure can ease even if crude stays elevated. The geopolitical premium driving today's oil move may prove volatile depending on how the conflict unfolds over the coming weeks.
